what.text: Benzoyl peroxide is an oxidizing agent put on the skin. FDA labels describe it as killing bacteria and loosening the outer skin layer (bactericidal and keratolytic). In the skin it is converted to benzoic acid, which leaves the body in urine.

In the US it is mainly an over-the-counter acne drug sold under FDA's acne monograph at 2.5% to 10%. A monograph is a rulebook that sets allowed ingredients, strengths and label wording; products that follow it do not need their own FDA approval. FDA has also approved prescription products that contain it, alone (Epsolay, for rosacea) or with adapalene, clindamycin, tretinoin or erythromycin.

research.text: Benzoyl peroxide has been studied in many trials, mostly short (up to 12 weeks) and often with a high or unclear risk of bias. A 2020 Cochrane review pooled 120 of them. The newest single-ingredient approval, Epsolay for rosacea, rests on two randomized trials. The 2024 to 2025 concern about benzene is covered under US position.

research.title: Topical benzoyl peroxide for acne (Cochrane review, Yang et al.)

facts.v: systematic review of randomized trials of benzoyl peroxide alone or combined, against placebo, no treatment or other creams
120 trials; 29,592 people randomized in 116 of them; mean ages 18 to 30
people's own rating of improvement; stopping because of side effects; any side effect

research.found: Low-certainty evidence suggested benzoyl peroxide may beat placebo or no treatment on self-rated improvement (risk ratio 1.27), with little or no difference against adapalene or clindamycin. People on it were more likely to stop because of side effects than with placebo (risk ratio 2.13), mostly for redness, itching and burning. Many trials had high or unclear risk of bias; 50 were industry funded.

research.found: 47.4% and 49.2% on Epsolay reached the goal, against 20.7% and 28.2% on vehicle cream. Inflamed spots fell by 17.4 and 20.3 on average, against 9.5 and 13.3.

research.text: The Epsolay label says benzoyl peroxide is well established as a tumor promoter in several animal species, but its meaning for people is unknown. Two-year skin studies in rats and mice did not show a significant rise in tumors. Bacterial gene tests gave mixed results, and it caused DNA strand breaks in mammalian cells. Fertility studies were not done. This is animal and lab evidence.

us.text: Benzoyl peroxide 2.5% to 10% is an over-the-counter acne drug under FDA's monograph (21 CFR 333.310). FDA has approved prescription products that contain it, and in 2025 tested acne products for benzene. As of November 1, 2026.

21 CFR part 333 subpart D lets benzoyl peroxide 2.5% to 10% be sold over the counter as an acne treatment if the product follows the monograph. The current wording of the benzoyl peroxide entry dates from a March 4, 2010 amendment (75 FR 9776). Required warnings include: do not use if you have very sensitive skin or are sensitive to benzoyl peroxide; avoid unnecessary sun and use sunscreen; avoid the eyes, lips and mouth; and stop and ask a doctor if irritation becomes severe.

us.text: On March 11, 2025, FDA reported testing 95 acne products containing benzoyl peroxide after a third-party lab reported high benzene levels. FDA found 6 products with elevated benzene; more than 90% had undetectable or extremely low levels. The makers agreed to recall affected lots at the retail level, and one more maker recalled a product after its own tests. FDA said that even with daily use for decades, the cancer risk from the benzene found is very low, and it warned that unvalidated test methods can overstate benzene levels.

us.text: FDA says benzene contamination in drugs may be linked to some inactive ingredients, such as carbomer thickeners, and that makers should not release any batch with more than 2 parts per million of benzene. FDA's recall records list 19 benzene-related recalls of benzoyl peroxide products: 15 begun in 2025 and 4 in 2026, all Class II.

world.lead: Benzoyl peroxide is sold without a prescription at low strengths in the US, Canada, the UK and Australia, and is authorised across the EU. Stronger strengths and combinations are prescription-only. It is not on the WADA Prohibited List.

after.text: Benzoyl peroxide is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List, in any class, in or out of competition. The 2027 list does not add it.

side.text: The common side effects are skin irritation: redness, dryness, peeling, burning, itching and sometimes swelling. Serious allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. It can make skin more sun-sensitive and bleaches hair and fabric.

items.text: The OTC monograph warns of redness, burning, itching, peeling or possibly swelling, and says to stop and ask a doctor if irritation becomes severe.

items.text: In the Epsolay trials (488 people), application site pain and redness each affected 2%, itching 1% and swelling 1%.
Anaphylaxis, angioedema and hives have been reported with benzoyl peroxide products. Allergic contact dermatitis can occur.
Benzoyl peroxide may increase sensitivity to sunlight.

unconfirmed: FDA's 2025 statement says it would publish its full benzene test results in peer-reviewed journals; that publication was not found or read.
Benzoyl peroxide's original US approval history and the older single-ingredient trials were not reviewed one by one.
An FDA safety communication on serious allergic reactions to OTC acne products was looked for on fda.gov but not found; allergy warnings here come from the Epsolay label.
surprises: FDA's own testing found elevated benzene in only 6 of 95 benzoyl peroxide products, fewer than a third-party lab had reported, and FDA called the cancer risk very low; recalls were at the retail level, not the consumer level.
The 2020 Cochrane review rated the evidence for benzoyl peroxide over placebo as low certainty, despite its long use.
